entries.effect: sets the dispatch queue that runs the operations, raising NSInvalidArgumentException when the queue is not empty, as the newest release does
entries.source: the host's own Foundation, held against the port's scheduler by tests/backports/host/underlying and read again on an iPhone 4S and an iPad 2 running 6.1.3 by tests/backports/device/underlying.m

entries.reason: the release runs an operation queue on threads of its own and cannot be told to run it on a dispatch queue, so the port schedules the operations of such a queue itself
entries.effect: with an underlying queue set, the queue's operations start on that dispatch queue, at most as many at a time as the limit allows, the ready ones by priority and then by arrival; the count, the operations, cancelling, suspending, waiting and +currentQueue answer for it; a queue that is not empty refuses a new underlying queue, and setting nil hands the queue back to the release

entries.reason: the release has no Low Power Mode: no setting turns it on and no process can read a state of it
entries.effect: it answers NO, as a device whose user has not turned the mode on does, and says so once in the log; an application is never told to save energy
